```spec.md
# Specification: single-player Battleship in the browser (Node.js server)

Status: written by the `spec` stage of an unattended ShipLoop run. Nothing is implemented. KNOWLEDGE/spec.md did not exist and the repository is empty, so every R-<n> below is **added** by this run. None is preserved or changed, and none is retired (see ## Retired). Acceptance lines are plans to confirm, not results.

## Reading guide

- Acceptance lines are written `R-<n>(x) kind — statement. Surface: <where observed>. Confirm: <how>.` Kind is positive, failure or boundary. A kind that would add nothing is written `n/a: <reason>`.
- Surfaces:
  - HTTP: the running server, over real sockets.
  - ENGINE: the rules module, driven directly from an explicit position (R-14).
  - PAGE-LOGIC: the page's script run under Node with stubbed fetch and storage. Stub responses are recorded from the real server in the W1 run, never hand-written.
  - BROWSER: a real browser. It is used only if the verify environment has one (intake OQ6).
  - STATIC: shipped files read, not run.
  - PROCESS: the documented commands run as child processes.
- Confirm:
  - T: automated test run by `npm test`, whose name begins with the line's label, e.g. `R-3(c)`.
  - P: scripted probe by the verify stage, outside the suite.
  - I: inspection.
  - Q: the requester, after the run returns.
- Not decided here. These are architecture-stage choices, recorded later as AD-<n> in KNOWLEDGE/architecture.md: routes, JSON field names, module layout, how the page and engine are split, the test runner, the shape of the seeding seam, the dependency policy, how CSS/JS are delivered. This spec fixes observable behaviour only.

## Vocabulary and fixtures (not requirements)

- **Board and cell token.** The board is 10×10. A cell token is one uppercase row letter A–J (A at the top) followed by a column number 1–10 without leading zero (left to right): `A1`, `B2`, `J10`. Not tokens: `K1`, `A0`, `A11`, `a1`, `A01`, `B`, the empty string.
- **Fleet.** Five ships: Carrier 5, Battleship 4, Cruiser 3, Submarine 3, Destroyer 2. That is 17 occupied cells.
- **Shot report.** Result is miss, hit or sunk. Only a sunk report carries the ship name.
- **Operations.** Logical names only; the architecture stage fixes routes and fields.
  - NEW-GAME (no input) returns a game id and the view.
  - GET-STATE (game id) returns the view.
  - FIRE (game id + cell token) returns the player-shot report, the computer-shot report (absent when the player's shot ended the game) and the view after both shots.
- **View.**
  - status (in-progress or over) and winner (player, computer or none);
  - the player's fleet with every computer shot on it;
  - the player's shots with results;
  - each side's sunk ships and remaining-ship count;
  - **counts** = (player shots, computer shots);
  - once over, the computer's whole fleet.
- **Statuses** (RFC 9110 meanings): 2xx accepted; 400 malformed or invalid; 404 unknown game or route; 405 wrong method; 409 well-formed but not allowed in the current state; 413 body too large.
- **Fleet ALPHA** (computer side in most tests). Rows A, C, D, E, F, H, J are used; rows B, G, I are empty.
  - Carrier A1 A2 A3 A4 A5
  - Battleship C1 D1 E1 F1
  - Cruiser H3 H4 H5
  - Submarine J8 J9 J10
  - Destroyer E8 F8
- **Fleet ALPHA-2.** Row B empty.
  - Carrier G1–G5
  - Battleship D10 E10 F10 G10
  - Cruiser C3 C4 C5
  - Submarine I6 I7 I8
  - Destroyer A9 A10
- **Fleet ALPHA-3.** A1 is a Carrier cell; A2 and B2 are empty.
  - Carrier A1 B1 C1 D1 E1
  - Battleship F3 F4 F5 F6
  - Cruiser H3 H4 H5
  - Submarine J8 J9 J10
  - Destroyer E8 F8
- **Fleet BRAVO** (player side). No two ships touch.
  - Carrier A10 B10 C10 D10 E10
  - Battleship G1 G2 G3 G4
  - Cruiser C3 C4 C5
  - Submarine I6 I7 I8
  - Destroyer F8 G8
- **Fleet BRAVO-T** (BRAVO transposed: row index and column number swapped).
  - Carrier J1–J5
  - Battleship A7 B7 C7 D7
  - Cruiser C3 D3 E3
  - Submarine F9 G9 H9
  - Destroyer H6 H7
- **Seed.** Given a seed, the computer's random choices (and fleet placement when no fleet is given) are a pure function of that seed.
- **Scripts.**
  - S-ROWMAJOR: FIRE A1…A10, B1…B10, …, J1…J10 in order, stopping at the first response whose status is over.
  - S-SAFE30: FIRE B1…B10, G1…G10, I1…I10. All 30 are misses on ALPHA.
- **Walk W1.** Computer fleet ALPHA, player fleet BRAVO, seed s1. s1 is the smallest seed in 1–20 for which the computer's first 17 replies include at least one miss; this precondition is read from the transcript, and the test fails if no seed qualifies.

| Accepted shot | Cell | Expected player report | Computer replies after | Computer ships left |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | B2 | miss | 1 | 5 |
| 2–5 | A1 A2 A3 A4 | hit | 2, 3, 4, 5 | 5 |
| 6 | A5 | hit, sunk Carrier | 6 | 4 |
| (attempt) | A1 again | refused, 409, counts stay (6,6) | 6 | 4 |
| 7–9 | C1 D1 E1 | hit | 7, 8, 9 | 4 |
| 10 | F1 | sunk Battleship | 10 | 3 |
| 11–12 | H3 H4 | hit | 11, 12 | 3 |
| 13 | H5 | sunk Cruiser | 13 | 2 |
| 14 | E8 | hit | 14 | 2 |
| 15 | F8 | sunk Destroyer | 15 | 1 |
| 16–17 | J8 J9 | hit | 16, 17 | 1 |
| 18 | J10 | sunk Submarine; game over, player wins | none (stays 17) | 0 |

  Totals: 18 accepted shots, 17 hits (5+4+3+2+3), 17 computer replies, final counts (18,17).
- **Position P-LOSS.**
  - Player fleet is BRAVO.
  - The computer has fired every BRAVO ship cell except G8 (16 hits): Carrier, Battleship, Cruiser and Submarine are sunk, and the Destroyer is hit at F8 only.
  - The player has fired 16 misses on ALPHA: B1–B10 and G1–G6.
  - The computer is to move.
  - It is reachable in principle: 16 consecutive computer hits.

## Defaults and assumptions (unattended; the requester may overturn; none blocks)

- Classic rules, as intake OQ1 records them:
  - 10×10 board and the fleet above.
  - Player moves first.
  - One shot per turn, no extra turn after a hit.
  - A sinking is announced.
- Ships may touch each other.
- Both fleets are placed randomly, and the player cannot rearrange (OQ2).
- The computer hunts around its hits and never peeks (OQ3).
- Cell tokens are strict uppercase.
- The first page load starts a game automatically.
- "New game" is immediate, with no confirmation.
- The page follows the OS light or dark setting, with no manual toggle.
- The default port is 3000.
- The exact message wording in R-11 is product copy.
- Classic rules come from general knowledge; research consulted no source.

## Request traceability

| Request outcome | Acceptance lines |
|---|---|
| S1 a Battleship game | R-2(a)(b), R-3(a)–(g), R-6(a)–(e) |
| S1 "small" | R-2(e) and the "Left out" lists |
| S1 "single-player" | R-2(e), R-10(h) |
| S1 "play in the browser" | R-1(a)(b), R-11(a)–(h), R-15(a)–(h) |
| S1 "against the computer" | R-4(a)–(d), R-5(a)–(c) |
| S2 "Node.js for the server" | R-1(e), R-16(a) |
| S2 "include tests" | R-12(a)–(d), R-14(a)–(c) |

Derived rather than asked: R-7–R-10 and R-13–R-16, from intake defaults and the domain rules of a hidden-information game.

## Requirements

### R-1 Start the server and serve the page
Primary: yes.
- Record:
  - basis: S1 "in the browser", S2 "Node.js for the server"; intake OUTCOMES (where played, server), BOUNDARIES (authority limits, entry points), OQ5.
  - preserved/changed: new.
  - locators: request S1–S2; intake as listed; discovery "Baseline".
  - evidence limits: no command has been run (no package.json exists).
  - pending: implementation; checks (a)–(f).
- Behaviour: the documented command `npm start` runs the server as a Node.js process that listens only on this machine, prints a line containing its URL, and serves the single game page and its assets at `http://localhost:<port>/`. The port comes from the PORT environment variable, default 3000. PORT=0 means any free port, and the printed URL shows the port actually bound.
- Left out: deployment, hosting, domains, TLS, process managers, global installs. The request grants none of them.
- Error behaviour: an occupied or invalid port makes the process exit with a message naming PORT. It does not hang.
- Consumer outcome: the requester runs the README command and opens the printed URL.
- Acceptance:
  - R-1(a) positive — in a fresh copy of the checkout, `npm start` with PORT=0 prints a line matching `http://localhost:<n>/` with n>0. A GET of that URL returns 2xx `text/html` whose `<title>` is `Battleship`. Surface: PROCESS+HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-1(b) positive — every same-origin URL referenced by the served HTML (stylesheet, script, icon) returns 2xx with a content type matching its file type. The URLs are parsed from the HTML, not hand-listed. Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-1(c) failure — with PORT held by another listener, and with PORT=`abc`, `-1` and `65536`, `npm start` exits non-zero and stderr names `PORT`. Surface: PROCESS. Confirm: T.
  - R-1(d) boundary — with PORT unset the printed URL is `http://localhost:3000/`. If 3000 is occupied in the verify environment, this line is NOT-REPLAYED there. Surface: PROCESS. Confirm: P.
  - R-1(e) positive — `scripts.start` in package.json begins with `node `, and the repository holds no server code for another runtime. Surface: STATIC. Confirm: I.
  - R-1(f) positive — README.md at the checkout root names `npm start`, `npm test`, the default URL and how to set PORT. Surface: STATIC. Confirm: I.
- Open gap: discovery reported Node.js 26, Python 3.13 and git, but no npm version. Default: the verify stage runs `npm --version` first. If npm is absent, it runs the `node` command lines inside package.json scripts directly, and the gap passes to the requester. Non-blocking.

### R-2 A new game: boards and fleets
Primary: yes.
- Record:
  - basis: S1; intake OQ1, OQ2.
  - preserved/changed: new.
  - locators: request S1; intake OUTCOMES S1 (what), OQ1, OQ2.
  - evidence limits: classic rules are not source-checked; random placement is checked by properties only.
  - pending: implementation; checks (a)–(f).
- Behaviour: NEW-GAME creates an independent game in status in-progress with the player to move and no shots. Each side has the five-ship fleet placed at random.
  - Placement rules: ships are straight (horizontal or vertical), fully inside A1–J10, and share no cell. Touching is allowed.
  - The response gives the game id and a view that shows the player's own fleet and omits the computer's.
- Left out: manual or drag placement, re-roll, other fleets or board sizes, rule variants (salvo, extra turn on hit), modes, difficulty selector, a second human, accounts, leaderboard, persistence, sound.
- State and data:
  - resource: one new game record, identity = the new game id.
  - invariants I1–I5 (R-3) hold from creation with zero shots.
  - recovery: none needed.
  - unknown: idle period (R-10).
- Acceptance:
  - R-2(a) positive — for seeds 1–1000, both generated fleets have exactly Carrier 5, Battleship 4, Cruiser 3, Submarine 3, Destroyer 2. Each ship is straight and inside the board, and the 17 cells are distinct. Surface: ENGINE. Confirm: T.
  - R-2(b) positive — NEW-GAME with seed 1 and no explicit fleet returns 2xx and an id. Status is in-progress, the player's fleet has the five ships by name and length, both shot lists are empty, counts are (0,0), and the computer fleet is absent (absence is proven by R-7(a)). Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-2(c) boundary — across seeds 1–100, more than one distinct computer layout occurs and the Carrier appears both horizontal and vertical. If placement is random, the chance of failure is below 2^-99. Surface: ENGINE. Confirm: T.
  - R-2(d) boundary — across the 2,000 fleets of seeds 1–1000 (both sides), each of the 100 cells, corners and edges included, is occupied at least once. This rules out placement that avoids the board's edges. Surface: ENGINE. Confirm: T.
  - R-2(e) boundary (single configuration) — the served page offers no control for mode, difficulty, board size, player count, name or login, save/load, sound or leaderboard. Its only controls are New game, the board cells and the Retry button of R-15(c). Surface: PAGE-LOGIC+STATIC. Confirm: T.
  - R-2(f) failure — n/a: refusing a client-supplied seed or fleet is specified once, in R-8(e).
- Open gap: rules variant, placement mode and "ships may touch" are defaults. Owner: the requester, after the first play. Non-blocking.

### R-3 The player's shot
Primary: yes.
- Record:
  - basis: S1; intake OQ1, OUTCOMES.
  - preserved/changed: new.
  - locators: request S1; intake OQ1.
  - evidence limits: W1 was walked on paper (see Walk record); computer replies are not computed.
  - pending: implementation; checks (a)–(g).
- Behaviour: while the game is in-progress, FIRE with an in-range token the player has not fired is accepted.
  - The server resolves it against the computer's fleet and reports miss, hit or sunk. Only sunk names the ship.
  - Then, unless the game is over, the computer replies (R-4).
  - The response carries both shot reports and the resulting view.
- Left out: salvos, extra turn after a hit, undo.
- Error behaviour: a repeated cell or a shot after game over gets 409; invalid input follows R-8. Refusals change no state and cause no computer shot.
- Consumer outcome: the player sees the result at once.
- State and data:
  - resource: the game record.
  - identity: the game id.
  - invariants before and after every FIRE:
    - I1 — each side's shots are distinct in-board cells.
    - I2 — a hit cell belongs to exactly one opposing ship.
    - I3 — a ship is sunk if and only if all its cells are shot.
    - I4 — while in-progress, both sides have at least one unsunk ship.
    - I5 — in-progress: counts are (n,n). Player won: (n,n−1). Computer won: (n,n).
  - recovery: a refused FIRE leaves everything unchanged.
  - applicable checks: R-3(d)(f)(g), R-6(e), R-9.
  - unknowns: none.
- Acceptance (W1 fixtures):
  - R-3(a) positive — W1 step 1, FIRE `B2`: accepted, the player report says miss with no ship name, counts (1,1). Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-3(b) positive — W1 step 2, FIRE `A1`: hit, and the shot report carries no ship name. Counts (2,2). Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-3(c) positive — W1 step 6, FIRE `A5`: sunk with ship `Carrier`. The view lists Carrier as the computer's only sunk ship and shows 4 remaining. After step 5 the sunk list was empty and 5 remained. Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-3(d) failure — after step 6, FIRE `A1` again returns 409. GET-STATE before and after the attempt is identical, and counts stay (6,6). Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-3(e) boundary — on a fresh ALPHA/BRAVO game, FIRE `A1`, `A10`, `J1`, `J10` are all accepted, with results hit, miss, miss, hit and counts (4,4). Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-3(f) positive — the view returned by FIRE is byte-equal to the view returned by GET-STATE immediately afterwards. The server is the only authority on shots. Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-3(g) positive — every row of the W1 table holds (results, sunk names, counts, ships left, and no reply after step 18). Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.

### R-4 The computer's reply
Primary: yes.
- Record:
  - basis: S1 "against the computer"; intake OUTCOMES, OQ3.
  - preserved/changed: new.
  - locators: request S1; intake S1 (who and against whom), OQ3.
  - evidence limits: reply cells depend on the seed and are not computed here (NOT-REPLAYED); the oracles are properties.
  - pending: implementation; checks (a)–(d).
- Behaviour: after each accepted player shot that does not end the game, the computer fires exactly one shot at a cell of the player's board it has not fired at. The result is resolved against the player's fleet and reported in the same response. The computer never moves twice running or after the game is over.
- Left out: extra computer turns, difficulty levels.
- Acceptance:
  - R-4(a) positive — NEW-GAME starts with computer shots 0, so the player moves first. In W1 the computer shot count equals the accepted player shot count n for n ≤ 17, and stays 17 after step 18. Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-4(b) positive — over seeds 1–20 with BRAVO and S-ROWMAJOR, each computer report has a valid token. The result is hit or sunk if and only if the cell is in BRAVO; sunk if and only if that shot completes a BRAVO ship, with that ship's name. The oracle is computed from BRAVO, not from the server. Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-4(c) failure — in those games no computer cell repeats and every cell is within A1–J10. Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-4(d) boundary — each of those games reaches status over at the latest after the player's 100th shot, with at most 100 computer shots. Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.

### R-5 The computer plays fairly and hunts
Primary: no (derived from intake OQ3).
- Record:
  - basis: intake OQ3, S1 "against the computer".
  - preserved/changed: new.
  - locators: intake OQ3.
  - evidence limits: strength is bounded below by the adjacency oracle only; no difficulty target exists.
  - pending: implementation; checks (a)–(c).
- Behaviour:
  - The computer chooses shots only from what it observed: its own shot results.
  - An unresolved hit is a computer hit on a player ship that is not yet sunk. While such a hit has an unfired orthogonal neighbour inside the board, the computer's next shot is one of those neighbours.
  - Otherwise it fires at any unfired cell.
- Left out: difficulty levels, probability-density play, cheating.
- Acceptance:
  - R-5(a) positive — seeds 1–20, BRAVO, S-ROWMAJOR. At every computer move the rule above holds, recomputed from the transcript and BRAVO. BRAVO's ships do not touch, so "unresolved" is unambiguous. The check must evaluate the rule at least once across the 20 games; otherwise the test reports the fixture inadequate. Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-5(b) positive (no peeking) — computer fleet ALPHA, player fleets BRAVO and BRAVO-T, seeds 1–20, script S-SAFE30. The computer's shot sequences are identical up to and including the first index where the shot reports differ. That index must exist for every seed, else the fixture is reported inadequate. Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-5(c) boundary — two positions, each with the computer to move:
    - Position 1: the computer fired only A10 (a Carrier hit), and the player fired B1, B2, B3. The next shot must be A9 or B10.
    - Position 2: the computer fired A9 (miss), A10 and B10 (both Carrier hits), and the player fired B1, B2, B3. The next shot must be C10 or B9.
    - Off-board neighbours and repeats are never chosen.
    - Surface: ENGINE. Confirm: T.
- Open gap: strength beyond adjacency (OQ3). Owner: the requester, after the first play. Non-blocking.

### R-6 Game end
Primary: yes.
- Record:
  - basis: S1; intake OQ1.
  - preserved/changed: new.
  - locators: intake OQ1, OUTCOMES hidden information.
  - evidence limits: the computer-win path is reached only through a constructed position (P-LOSS), not through an HTTP game.
  - pending: implementation; checks (a)–(e).
- Behaviour: the game ends the moment all five ships of one side are sunk. That side loses. Status becomes over and the winner is named. No further shot from either side is accepted. The computer's whole fleet is revealed. The page announces the result (R-11).
- Left out: scoring, rematch inside the same game.
- Acceptance:
  - R-6(a) positive — W1 step 18 (`J10`): sunk Submarine, status over, winner player, no computer report, counts (18,17). The view's computer fleet equals ALPHA exactly (5 ships, names, cells compared as sets), and GET-STATE agrees. Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-6(b) positive — P-LOSS, apply the computer shot `G8`: sunk Destroyer, status over, winner computer, computer fleet revealed. Surface: ENGINE. Confirm: T.
  - R-6(c) failure — after W1 ends, FIRE `G7` (valid, unfired) returns 409. GET-STATE before and after is identical and counts stay (18,17). In P-LOSS after the computer wins, a player shot is refused. Surface: HTTP, ENGINE. Confirm: T.
  - R-6(d) boundary — after W1 step 17 (`J9`): status in-progress, computer sunk list Carrier, Battleship, Cruiser, Destroyer, 1 ship remaining, computer fleet not revealed, counts (17,17). Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-6(e) boundary — for every seed-1–20 game (R-4(b) setup) at game over, exactly one side has all ships sunk and it is the declared loser. The winner has at least one unsunk ship. I5 holds throughout. Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.

### R-7 Hidden information
Primary: no (inherent to the game; intake OUTCOMES, hidden information).
- Record:
  - basis: intake hidden information, S2 tests clause.
  - preserved/changed: new.
  - locators: intake INTERACTION AND STATE.
  - evidence limits: non-interference is shown for the tested fleet pairs.
  - pending: implementation; checks (a)–(d).
- Behaviour:
  - Until the game is over, nothing delivered to the browser reveals the contents of any computer cell the player has not fired at.
  - A hit names no ship and shows no orientation. A sunk ship's name and cells may be shown, because every cell is already hit.
  - The computer's choices are made on the server.
  - The player's own fleet is visible to the player and is never used by the computer to aim (R-5(b)).
- Acceptance:
  - R-7(a) positive (non-interference, all misses) — seed 1, player fleet BRAVO, computer fleets ALPHA and ALPHA-2. Calls: NEW-GAME, GET-STATE, then FIRE `B2`, `B4`, `B6`, `B8`, `B10`, each followed by GET-STATE. Every response body in game 1 equals the corresponding body in game 2 after the game id string is replaced by a placeholder. Non-vacuity: the fleets differ, and all five shots are misses in both. Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-7(b) positive (a hit leaks nothing) — computer fleets ALPHA and ALPHA-3, same seed and BRAVO. Calls: NEW-GAME, FIRE `B2`, FIRE `A1`, GET-STATE, FIRE `A2`. A1 is a hit in both; A2 is a hit in ALPHA and a miss in ALPHA-3. Responses to the first four calls are identical, the response to FIRE `A2` differs, and the divergence must occur. Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-7(c) failure — `GET /` and each page asset are byte-identical before any game exists and after games exist, and the client assets contain no pseudo-random or crypto source (`Math.random`, `crypto.`). The client cannot generate or decide hidden state. Surface: HTTP+STATIC. Confirm: T.
  - R-7(d) boundary — server stdout and stderr captured during R-7(a) contain neither the game id nor any request body text. Surface: PROCESS. Confirm: T.

### R-8 Input validation and error behaviour
Primary: no (derived).
- Record:
  - basis: S2 tests clause; intake OQ4.
  - preserved/changed: new.
  - locators: intake OQ4, Risks.
  - evidence limits: the cell token is the logical encoding; the architecture stage maps it onto the wire.
  - pending: implementation; checks (a)–(g).
- Behaviour: any request the server cannot honour is refused with the status of the vocabulary, a machine-readable reason and a short human message. A refusal changes no game state, makes no computer shot, creates no game, and leaves the server running.
- Acceptance:
  - R-8(a) failure — on a live game, FIRE with each of these returns 400, with GET-STATE before and after identical and counts unchanged: `K1`, `A0`, `A11`, `a1`, `A01`, the empty string, `B`, `B2x`, null, the number 12, a missing cell member, an extra member, a non-JSON body, a JSON array body. Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-8(b) failure — GET-STATE and FIRE with game ids `no-such-game`, the empty id, `../../etc/passwd` and a 4,096-character id all return 404 and create no state. Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-8(c) failure — `/api/nope` returns 404. Each operation with a wrong method (GET on NEW-GAME, POST on GET-STATE, DELETE on any) returns 405. Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-8(d) boundary — a FIRE with a 1 MiB (1,048,576-byte) body returns 413, and the server then answers GET-STATE on a live game normally. A valid FIRE of about 100 bytes is accepted. The exact limit between the two is unresolved (open gap). Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-8(e) failure — NEW-GAME with any body member (`{"seed":1}`, `{"fleet":[]}`, `{"x":1}`) returns 400 and returns no game id. An empty body and `{}` are accepted. Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-8(f) failure — no error body above contains the checkout's absolute path, `node_modules`, or `    at ` (a stack line). Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-8(g) boundary — after (a)–(e), the full W1 replay still passes and stderr shows no uncaught exception. Surface: HTTP+PROCESS. Confirm: T.
- Open gap: the request-body limit is not set by the request. Owner: the architecture stage, which sets it between the two probes above. Non-blocking.

### R-9 Atomic turns, simultaneous requests and the page–server boundary
Primary: no (derived).
- Record:
  - basis: intake lifetime and shared state; stage guidance 7–9.
  - preserved/changed: new.
  - locators: intake INTERACTION AND STATE.
  - evidence limits: race tests detect only what the scheduler exposes; (d) is best-effort.
  - pending: implementation; checks (a)–(d).
- Behaviour:
  - A FIRE is atomic: the player's shot and the computer's reply are applied together. No response or GET-STATE shows the player's shot without the reply while the game is in-progress.
  - Requests for one game are applied one at a time in arrival order (no lost update, no partial turn). Different games are independent.
- Service boundary (page to server, the only one):
  - Current authority: the server record decides every result; the page holds the id and a rendering of the last view (R-3(f), R-7(c)).
  - Freshness versus revocation: n/a, no grants. The id is a bearer token, and an expired or restarted game gets 404 at once (R-10(e)(f)).
  - Incremental state: n/a, every response carries the full view, with no deltas or streams.
  - Async completion and recovery: FIRE completes inside its request. If the response is lost, the shot may be recorded, and the page re-reads with GET-STATE (R-11(f)).
  - Owned event coverage: n/a, the server emits no events.
- Acceptance:
  - R-9(a) positive — two concurrent FIRE `B2` on one fresh ALPHA/BRAVO game give exactly one 2xx and one 409, final counts (1,1). Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.

### R-10 Game lifecycle and state ownership
Primary: no (derived from intake lifetime and reload decisions).
- Record:
  - basis: intake INTERACTION AND STATE (lifetime, shared state).
  - preserved/changed: new. Refinement of intake's wording: "New game" makes the old record unreachable from the page, and the server removes it at idle expiry rather than at once.
  - locators: intake lifetime, actors and identity, what the runtime provides.
  - evidence limits: reload, second-tab and duplicated-tab behaviour is real only in a browser.
  - pending: implementation; checks (a)–(h).
- Behaviour: no accounts or sharing. A first page load starts a game, and a reload resumes it. A page opened fresh in a second tab starts its own game. "New game" starts a fresh game at any time. A game whose record is gone yields a visible notice and a fresh game.
- State items:

| State | Owner and location | Who may read | Simultaneous changes | Ends and is removed by | Quotas met |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Game record | server process memory, keyed by game id | whoever presents the id; the computer fleet only once over | serial, arrival order (R-9) | idle expiry; server restart. Over keeps it readable until expiry | process memory: no numeric cap set, bounded only by idle expiry (gap) |
| Game id on the client | per-tab browser storage, written by the page | the page | one writer per tab | tab closed; replaced by New game; discarded on 404 | one short string |
| Rendered page state | page memory | the requester | rebuilt from the view | reload or close | n/a |

- Personal or secret data: none is collected, shown, stored, logged or kept. Nothing needs removal beyond the rows above.
- Recovery: losing a record is by design. The next request gets 404, and the page starts a fresh game. No partial state can exist, because turns are atomic (R-9).
- Acceptance:
  - R-10(a) positive — with empty storage the page sends exactly one NEW-GAME, stores the id and renders the returned view. Surface: PAGE-LOGIC (BROWSER if available). Confirm: T.
  - R-10(b) positive — with a stored live id the page sends GET-STATE with that id and no NEW-GAME, and renders the same shots and status. Over HTTP, GET-STATE after several FIREs equals the last FIRE's view. Surface: PAGE-LOGIC+HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-10(c) failure — a stored id answered 404: the page discards it, shows `Your previous game is no longer available. A new game has started.`, sends NEW-GAME once and shows fresh boards. Surface: PAGE-LOGIC. Confirm: T.
  - R-10(d) positive — "New game" sends NEW-GAME, stores the new id and shows fresh boards. Two games created from one client are independent (R-9(c)). Surface: PAGE-LOGIC. Confirm: T.
  - R-10(e) boundary — with an idle period of 1 s (test option), game X read at t≈0 returns 2xx, and after 2 s without requests returns 404. Game Y polled every 0.4 s for 2.4 s stays 2xx. Margins of at least 2× avoid edge flakiness. Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-10(f) failure — instance 1 creates a game and stops. Instance 2 starts on the same port. GET-STATE with the old id returns 404. Surface: HTTP+PROCESS. Confirm: T.
  - R-10(g) boundary — after W1 ends, GET-STATE returns 2xx (status over) immediately and at 0.5 s with a 1 s idle period, and 404 after 2 s idle. Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-10(h) boundary — two page instances with separate storage each send NEW-GAME and hold different ids. In a real browser, a second tab opened by URL starts its own game. Duplicated-tab behaviour is not specified. Surface: PAGE-LOGIC (BROWSER). Confirm: T, Q.
- Open gap: the default idle period is not derivable from the request. Owner: the architecture stage proposes it and the requester may tune it; tests use 1 s. No cap on simultaneous games is set (see exclusions). Non-blocking.

## Non-functional requirements

Operating conditions: the requester's own machine, one local user, loopback only, current evergreen browsers. No hosted instance exists.

### R-13 Local-only operation, privacy and abuse resistance
- Record:
  - basis: intake BOUNDARIES (authority limits), RISKS; stage guidance 7–9.
  - preserved/changed: new.
  - locators: intake authority limits, hidden information.
  - evidence limits: host-dependent items are marked below.
  - pending: implementation; checks (a)–(e).
- Acceptance:
  - R-13(a) positive — a server started through the production start path accepts connections on 127.0.0.1 or ::1 and refuses them on any non-loopback local address of the host. If the host has none, that half is NOT-REPLAYED on it. The listen call also names a loopback host explicitly. Surface: PROCESS+STATIC. Confirm: T, I.
  - R-13(b) positive — server source (excluding tests) uses no outbound-capable API (`http.request`, `https`, `fetch`, `net.connect`, `dns`, `child_process`). All shipped page assets reference only relative same-origin URLs: no `http:`, `https:`, `//host`, CDN, web fonts or analytics. The page's own `fetch` calls use relative URLs. Surface: STATIC. Confirm: T.
  - R-13(c) failure (static confinement) — with a raw HTTP client that does not normalise paths, GET of `/package.json`, `/README.md`, every other checkout file not declared as a page asset (derived from the filesystem), and `/../package.json`, `/%2e%2e/package.json`, `/..%2fpackage.json`, `/..\package.json`, `/assets/../../package.json`, `//etc/passwd`, `/%00` never returns 2xx, and no body contains the string `"scripts"`. Surface: HTTP. Confirm: T.
  - R-13(d) positive — 1,000 NEW-GAME calls give 1,000 distinct ids that are not in sorted order and not derived from a counter or the time. Id generation uses the platform's cryptographically secure source, not `Math.random`. Surface: HTTP+STATIC. Confirm: T, I.
  - R-13(e) positive (privacy) — no response during the W1 replay and the R-8 battery sets a cookie (no `Set-Cookie`). The page's only client-side write is the game id. Surface: HTTP+PAGE-LOGIC. Confirm: T.
- Open gap: the id's entropy bound is not set by the request. Owner: the architecture stage, from primary documentation. Non-blocking.
- Assessed residual: a hostile web page can start games on the loopback server but cannot read an existing game without its id, and there is no secret or personal data to protect. Further hardening (authentication, TLS, extra headers) is excluded; see the exclusions table.

### Exclusions and assessed-but-unbounded concerns

| Concern | Decision and reason |
|---|---|
| Latency and throughput | Excluded as numbers: the request states none, and each action touches at most 100 cells. The rule-derived bound is at most 100 shots per side (R-4(d)). |
| Capacity, scale, game cap | Unresolved bound: one local user, memory bounded only by idle expiry (R-10 gap). No cap is invented. |
| Availability and durability | By design a restart loses all games (R-10(f)). No SLO is requested. |
| Authentication, accounts, authorization beyond the id | Excluded: single local player, no personal data. The unguessable id is the capability (R-13(d)). |
| TLS, extra security headers, CSRF and DNS-rebinding hardening | Excluded: loopback only, no secrets (R-13 assessed residual). |
| Persistence, backup, history | Excluded: the request has none (R-10). |
| Observability beyond startup and error logs | Excluded: unrequested. Logs avoid ids and bodies (R-7(d)). |
| Internationalisation | Excluded: English only. |
| Deployment, release, rollback, domains, paid services | Out of scope: not granted by the request. |
| Licensing artefacts | Excluded: no third-party assets ship (R-13(b)), and no licence file is requested. |

- Method: paper walk from the stated start, with no helper and no execution. Each action was checked against the rule that permits it; each outcome was recomputed from the actions.
- W1:
  - Start: NEW-GAME through the R-14 seam, reachable by any local test client with no authority needed.

  - Recomputed result: 18 accepted shots, 17 hits, sinks at steps 6, 10, 13, 15, 18, final counts (18,17).

- P-LOSS and the R-5(c) positions are constructed, and each is reachable in principle by legal play.
- R-7(a) and (b): the shots are legal in both games. The computer sees identical observations, so its replies are identical until the first divergence. Row B is empty in ALPHA and ALPHA-2, and A2 is the first differing cell for ALPHA versus ALPHA-3.
- R-5(b): ALPHA uses rows A, C, D, E, F, H, J, so S-SAFE30's cells are all misses. BRAVO and BRAVO-T differ on 32 cells, so a divergence within 30 computer shots is overwhelmingly likely, and the test asserts it.
- NOT-REPLAYED (left open, no execution claimed):
  - computer reply cells under any seed;
  - `npm start` and `npm test` exit codes and case counts (no package.json exists);
  - layout overflow at 320 and 1280 px (no rendering engine);
  - non-loopback refusal on a host with no non-loopback address;
  - WCAG figures (recalled, not re-fetched).
```
